Ham and Cheese Crepes for Candlemas

Served at: Candlemas (Feast of the Presentation)

Serves 4-6 (makes about 12-15 crepes)Prep 20 minCook 45 min

Candlemas, or La Chandeleur, celebrated on February 2nd, marks the presentation of Jesus at the Temple and is traditionally associated with light and purification. In France, it's a beloved custom to make and eat crêpes on this day, symbolizing prosperity and the return of longer, sunnier days. Savory Ham and Cheese Crêpes are a classic choice, offering a comforting and delicious meal perfect for sharing with family.

Ingredients

  • 1 cup (120 g) all-purpose flour
  • 2 large eggs
  • 1 1/2 cups (360 ml) whole milk
  • 2 tablespoons (28 g) unsalted butter, melted, plus more for cooking
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt
  • 2 tablespoons (28 g) unsalted butter (for béchamel)
  • 2 tablespoons (15 g) all-purpose flour (for béchamel)
  • 1 1/2 cups (360 ml) whole milk, warmed (for béchamel)
  • Pinch of freshly grated nutmeg (optional)
  • Salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
  • 8 ounces (225 g) cooked ham, thinly sliced or diced
  • 8 ounces (225 g) Gruyère or Emmental cheese, grated

Method

  1. Prepare the Crêpe Batter: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour and salt. In a separate bowl, whisk the eggs and milk. Gradually add the wet ingredients to the dry ingredients, whisking until smooth. Stir in the 2 tablespoons of melted butter. Cover the bowl and let the batter rest in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes, or up to 2 hours.
  2. Make the Béchamel Sauce: While the batter rests, melt 2 tablespoons of butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Add the flour and whisk constantly for 1-2 minutes to create a roux. Gradually whisk in the warm milk, a little at a time, ensuring no lumps form. Continue to whisk until the sauce thickens to your desired consistency, about 5-7 minutes. Season with nutmeg (if using), salt, and pepper. Keep warm over very low heat, stirring occasionally, or set aside and gently reheat later.
  3. Cook the Crêpes: Heat an 8-inch (20 cm) non-stick crêpe pan or skillet over medium heat. Lightly grease the pan with a small amount of melted butter. Pour about 1/4 cup (60 ml) of batter into the center of the hot pan, immediately tilting and swirling the pan to spread the batter evenly into a thin circle. Cook for 1-2 minutes until the edges are golden and the crêpe easily lifts. Flip and cook for another 30-60 seconds on the second side. Transfer the cooked crêpe to a plate and repeat with the remaining batter, stacking the crêpes as you go.
  4. Assemble the Crêpes: Lay a cooked crêpe flat. Spread a thin layer of béchamel sauce over one half of the crêpe. Sprinkle a generous amount of grated cheese over the sauce, then top with some ham slices or diced ham.
  5. Fold and Heat: Fold the crêpe in half, then in half again to form a triangle, or simply roll it up. You can serve them immediately, or for a warmer, melted cheese experience, place the assembled crêpes on a baking sheet. Bake in a preheated oven at 350°F (175°C) for 5-10 minutes, or until the cheese is melted and bubbly. Alternatively, heat them gently in a skillet.
  6. Serve: Serve the warm Ham and Cheese Crêpes immediately, perhaps with a side salad.

Tips

  • For extra flavor, add a pinch of dried herbs like chives or parsley to the béchamel sauce.
  • Ensure your crêpe batter is well-rested; this allows the flour to fully hydrate, resulting in more tender crêpes.
  • If you don't have a crêpe pan, a good quality non-stick skillet works perfectly.
